db-er-tables-06: Do cheezein gino: kitni strong entities hain, aur kaun se relationships ko apni table chahiye. **Ternary** aur 1:N ka rule alag hai.
Rule: strong entity = 1 table, M:N ya ternary = 1 table, 1:N = sirf FK on the many side (koi table nahi).
AdmittedTo me 'many' side Patient hai, to `wid` Patient table me FK ban jaata hai. Ab entities aur Prescribes jodo. Trap: ternary ko teen binary tables me todna.
db-er-tables-07: Dono relationships **recursive** hain (entity apne aap se juda), par cardinality alag hai: Supervises 1:N, PrereqOf M:N.
Recursive me bhi same rule: 1:N → FK same table me (jaise `sup_eid`), M:N → alag table jisme do role columns hon.
Employee table me `sup_eid` column daal do, to Supervises ki table nahi chahiye. Ab PrereqOf ke liye socho. Trap: har role ke liye entity ki copy bana dena.
db-er-tables-08: Do rules ek saath lag rahe hain: Section **weak** hai (apni poori key nahi), aur `room` **multivalued** hai.
Weak entity ki key = owner key + partial key. Multivalued attribute ki table = (us entity ki poori key, value), aur key me dono aate hain.
Pehle Section ki poori key likho: `cid` + `sec_no`. Ab socho ek section ke do rooms ke liye do rows kaise alag hongi. Trap: `sec_no` ko akela key maan lena.
db-er-tables-09: List banao: kaun si entities merge ho sakti hain (1:1 + total **dono** sides), kaun se relationships FK me ghus jaate hain, aur kya alag table maangta hai.
Rules: 1:1 total both → 1 merged table; 1:N aur identifying relationship → FK; M:N, weak entity, multivalued attribute → har ek ki apni table.
Person aur Passport ek table ban gaye. Publishes 1:N hai, to `pubid` Book me jaata hai. Ab Book, Publisher, Writes, Edition, `format` gino. Trap: weak entity ka multivalued attribute bhool jaana.
db-er-tables-10: Cardinality 1:1 hai, par participation alag: Car **total**, Employee partial. Har statement ko is fark se judge karo.
1:1 me FK kisi bhi side ja sakta hai. Total side pe FK NOT NULL ho sakta hai; FK pe UNIQUE na ho to wo 1:N ban jaata hai. Merge sirf total-total pe.
Car me `eid` rakho: kya koi car bina employee ke hai? Phir socho kya ek employee do cars le sakta hai agar UNIQUE na ho. Trap: 1:1 dekhte hi merge kar dena.
db-er-tables-11: Paanch tarah ke attributes hain: key, **composite**, simple, **derived**, **multivalued**. Har ek ka mapping rule alag hai.
Composite → uske parts alag columns; derived → store nahi hota; multivalued → apni alag table (cid, phone).
`cid` aur `dob` seedhe columns hain. Ab `name` todo aur `age`, `phone` ka faisla karo. Trap: derived `age` ko bhi column bana dena.
db-er-tables-12: Chaar relationships hain; pehle har ek ki cardinality pehchano: kaun M:N hai, kaun 1:N, kaun 1:1.
Minimum tables = strong entities + M:N relationships (+ weak entities, multivalued attributes, agar hon). 1:N aur partial 1:1 sirf FK hote hain.
BelongsTo ke liye Instructor me `dept_id` aur Heads ke liye Department me `head_iid` daal do. Ab bachi tables gino. Trap: 1:1 ko alag table dena.
db-er-tables-13: Sawaal ye hai ki teen binary tables ternary fact ko wapas bana sakti hain ya nahi. Pehle SP, PJ, SJ ki rows likh lo.
Har fact (s, p, j) se teen pairs bante hain: (s,p), (p,j), (s,j). Join me koi triple tabhi aata hai jab uske teeno pairs apni-apni table me hon.
SP = {(s1,p1), (s1,p2), (s2,p1)}. Ab har option ke teeno pairs check karo. Trap: maan lena ki projections se original hamesha wapas mil jaata hai.
db-er-tables-14: Payment **weak** entity hai: `pay_no` sirf ek loan ke andar unique hai, poori table me nahi.
Weak entity ki table ki key = owner ki key + partial key.
Socho: loan L1 aur loan L2 dono ka payment 1 hai, to `pay_no` akela kaafi hai? Owner Loan ki key kya hai? Trap: extra non-key attribute key me daal dena.
db-er-tables-15: Har construct ko alag gino: strong entities, weak entity, do M:N relationships, aur Guest ke **do** multivalued attributes.
Tables = strong + weak + M:N + (har multivalued attribute ki ek table). Identifying relationship ki table nahi banti.
Strong entities 3 aur weak Room 1. Ab Stays, Uses aur dono multivalued attributes jodo. Trap: `phone` aur `email` ko ek hi table me daal dena.
db-er-tables-16: Har option ke liye poochho: kya ise kisi existing entity table ke ek column me rakha ja sakta hai, bina 1NF tode?
Rule: ek cell me ek hi value. Jahan ek entity ke liye kai values ya kai partners hon aur dono taraf 'many' ho, wahan alag table chahiye.
1:N lo: 'many' side ki har row ka sirf ek partner hai, to FK column kaafi. Isi tarah baaki teen judge karo. Trap: derived attribute ko stored maan lena.
db-keys-08: Teen candidate keys hain, to superkeys ke teen overlapping groups banenge. Do keys ke formula se kaam nahi chalega; teen sets ka inclusion-exclusion chahiye.
$|K_1 \cup K_2 \cup K_3| = \sum |K_i| - \sum |K_i \cap K_j| + |K_1 \cap K_2 \cap K_3|$, jahan har term = $2^{4-(\text{fixed attributes})}$.
Singles: {A} → $2^3=8$, {B} → 8, {C, D} → $2^2=4$. Ab pairs ke union sets {A,B}, {A,C,D}, {B,C,D} gino. Trap: teeno wala term add back karna bhool jaana.
db-keys-09: Do keys B share karti hain. Overlap wo sets hain jo **dono** keys ko contain karte hain, yani {A, B} ∪ {B, C} ke supersets.
{A, B} ke supersets: baaki 3 attributes free, $2^3 = 8$. {B, C} ke bhi utne. Ab overlap {A, B, C} ke liye nikalo. Trap: overlap ke liye $K_1 \cap K_2$ = {B} le lena.
db-keys-10: Ek instance kisi set ko key **prove** nahi kar sakta, sirf rule out kar sakta hai: agar do rows me us set ki values same hon.
Rule: set X rule out hota hai jab do alag rows X pe same hon. Har option ke liye X ki values ki list bana kar repeat dhundo.
`name` column: Asha, Ravi, Asha, Meena — repeat hai. Ab `phone`, `city` aur pair wale option ke liye same check karo. Trap: sirf pehli do rows dekh kar faisla karna.
db-keys-11: FK apni hi table ko point karti hai aur action CASCADE hai, to ek delete ek chain shuru kar sakta hai: manager gaya to uske reports bhi jaayenge, phir unke reports bhi.
Levels me socho: level 0 = e1; agla level = jinka `mgr` pichhle level me hai. Chain tab rukti hai jab naya koi row na mile.
e1 delete hua; `mgr = e1` wale rows e2 aur e4 hain, wo bhi gaye. Ab e2 aur e4 ke reports dhundo, aur aage badho. Trap: chain ko ek level ke baad rok dena.
db-keys-12: Har insert pe do checks lagte hain: composite **primary key** (sid, cid) ka pair naya hai ya nahi, aur dono **foreign keys** existing rows ko point karti hain ya nahi.
PK (sid, cid): poora pair repeat nahi ho sakta, akela `sid` repeat ho sakta hai. FK: `sid` ∈ Student = {s1, s2, s3}, `cid` ∈ Course = {c1, c2}.
('s1', 'c2') lo: s1 Student me hai, c2 Course me, aur pair Enroll me pehle se nahi. Isi tarah baaki teen jaancho. Trap: `sid` repeat dekh kar PK violation maan lena.
db-keys-13: Candidate key **minimal** hoti hai, to koi key kisi doosri key ka subset nahi ho sakti. Sawaal hai: aise kitne sets ek saath ho sakte hain?
Ek hi size ke alag sets kabhi ek doosre ke subset nahi hote. To size k chuno jahan $\binom{4}{k}$ sabse bada ho.
Size 1 lo: {A}, {B}, {C}, {D} → $\binom{4}{1}=4$ keys. Ab size 2 aur 3 ke liye $\binom{4}{k}$ nikal kar compare karo. Trap: saare subsets gin lena.
db-keys-14: Do test lagao: (1) kya set kisi candidate key ko contain karta hai? (2) kya usme se koi attribute hata kar bhi key bachi rehti hai?
Superkey ⇔ set ⊇ {A} ya set ⊇ {B, C}. Candidate key ⇔ superkey + minimal (koi proper subset superkey nahi).
{B} lo: kya ye {A} ya {B, C} ko contain karta hai? Phir har option pe pehle superkey test, phir minimality. Trap: candidate key ko hi 'non-minimal superkey' maan lena.
db-keys-15: Ek hi column `did` pe do constraints hain: FK action **SET NULL** aur **NOT NULL**. Dekho delete ke baad dono ek saath satisfy ho sakte hain ya nahi.
ON DELETE SET NULL: matching child rows me FK = NULL likha jaata hai. Agar wo likhna kisi constraint ko todta hai to poora statement fail hota hai.
d1 delete karne pe e1 aur e3 ke `did` ko NULL banana padega. Ab NOT NULL se compare karo. Trap: SET NULL ko CASCADE samajh lena.
db-keys-16: Teen definitions yaad karo: superkey, candidate key (minimal superkey), primary key (chuni hui candidate key). Har statement ko definition se check karo.
Minimal ka matlab: koi bhi attribute hatao to superkey nahi rehta. 'Always' wale statement ke liye ek counterexample kaafi hai.
Statement 4 ke liye socho: R(A, B, C) jisme sirf {A, B, C} hi key ho — kya isme chhoti key hai? Baaki teen bhi isi tarah judge karo. Trap: candidate keys aur primary key ki ginti mix karna.
db-ra-eval-07: R aur S me **do** common columns hain: B aur C. Natural join dono pe ek saath equality maangta hai.
Size $= \sum_{(b,c)}$ (R me (b,c) ki count) × (S me (b,c) ki count), sirf un pairs pe jo dono me hon.
Pair (x, p): R me 1 row (A = 1), S me 2 rows (D = 10, 20) → 2 tuples. Ab (x, q), (y, p), (y, q), (z, q) karo. Trap: sirf B pe join kar dena.
db-ra-eval-08: Do operations hain: pehle Cartesian product, phir sirf A pe **projection**. Relational algebra set semantics follow karta hai.
$\pi_A$ duplicate tuples hata deta hai. Agar S khaali nahi hai to $\pi_A(R \times S)$ me har A value jo R me hai, ek baar aati hai.
Product me 4 × 5 = 20 rows bani, columns (A, B, C). Ab sirf A column rakho aur repeats hatao. Trap: 20 hi likh dena.
db-ra-eval-09: Teen joins ki baat ho rahi hai: inner, left outer, right outer. Sabse pehle inner join ka size nikalo, baaki uspe add hote hain.
Left outer = inner + R ke unmatched rows (C = NULL). Right outer = inner + S ke unmatched rows (A = NULL).
B = a: R me 2 rows, S me 2 rows → 4 tuples. Ab B = c add karo, phir dekho R ke kaun se B values S me nahi hain. Trap: right join me S ka unmatched row bhool jaana.
db-ra-division-05: Division ka matlab 'har ek': wo pilots chahiye jo Fleet ke **saare** planes pe certified hain.
Har pilot ka plane-set banao aur check karo: kya {A320, B737, ATR} ⊆ us pilot ka set?
p1 ka set {A320, B737, ATR} hai, to p1 pass. Ab p2, p3, p4 ke sets likh kar check karo. Trap: extra plane (Q400) wale pilot ko fail kar dena.
db-ra-division-06: NewFleet me ek plane E190 hai jo Cert me kahin nahi dikhta. Division me divisor ki **har** value cover honi chahiye.
Product me (p1, E190), (p2, E190), ... sab aayenge. Inme se kaun se Cert me hain? Usse decide karo kaun bachta hai. Trap: E190 ko ignore kar dena.
db-ra-division-07: Division ki definition yaad karo: a result me hai agar R me (a, b) har b ∈ S ke liye ho. Har statement ko isi definition se test karo.
'Always' ke liye: sahi ho to definition se proof, galat ho to ek chhota counterexample (1–2 rows) kaafi hai.
Statement 2 lo: $S_2$ bada hai, to $S_2$ ki har value cover karna mushkil hai ya aasaan? Statement 4 ke liye S me ek value aur R me do a values try karo. Trap: join ko division samajhna.
db-ra-division-08: Keyword **'every'** hai, to division ya ∀ chahiye. Join sirf 'kam se kam ek' deta hai.
$R(A, B) \div S(B)$: R me (sid, cid) pairs, S me sirf wo cids jo **har** student ko lene hain.
Divisor banao: Course se pehle CS wale rows chuno, phir sirf `cid` rakho. Ab dekho kaun sa option ise sahi side pe use karta hai. Trap: CS selection chhod dena.
db-ra-division-09: Ye relation 'missing pairs' hai: har employee × har needed skill, minus jo pairs Works me sach me hain.
Size = $|\pi_{eid}(\text{Works})| \times |\text{Need}|$ − (Works ke wo rows jo product me hain).
Distinct eids 4 hain aur Need me 3 skills, to product me 12 pairs. Ab gino Works ke kitne rows inme aate hain. Trap: final division ka size bata dena.
db-ra-equiv-06: Ye **selection pushdown** ka sawaal hai: join se pehle condition ko us table pe lagana jisme uske attributes hain.
Rules: $\sigma_{p \land q} = \sigma_p(\sigma_q(\cdot))$, aur $\sigma_p$ join ke andar sirf us side jaa sakta hai jisme p ke saare attributes hon.
A sirf R me hai, C sirf S me. To AND ke do hisse alag-alag kahan jaayenge? Ab har option me join condition aur AND/OR dekho. Trap: ⋈ ki jagah × likh dena.
db-ra-equiv-07: 'Always' ka matlab: har instance pe. Har equivalence ke liye ya to element-wise argument do, ya ek chhota counterexample banao.
π ∪ pe distribute karta hai, par ∩ ya − pe nahi. σ ek row-by-row filter hai. Difference ke liye associativity alag se check karo.
∩ wala test karo: R = {(1, x)}, S = {(1, y)} lo aur dono sides nikalo. Last option ke liye S = ∅ aur R = T try karo. Trap: π ko ∩ pe bhi distribute maan lena.
db-ra-equiv-08: 'Both c1 and c2' ek student ke **do alag rows** ki baat hai. Socho ek single tuple me `cid` ki kitni values ho sakti hain.
Ek σ har tuple ko akela test karta hai. Do alag rows ko jodne ke liye do sets bana kar ∩ karo, ya rename karke self-join.
Option B lo: kya koi ek row hai jisme cid = 'c1' bhi ho aur cid = 'c2' bhi? Ab baaki options me ∩, ∪, − ka matlab socho. Trap: AND ko 'dono courses' padh lena.
db-ra-equiv-09: Order dhyan se padho: pehle **R − S** (poore tuples pe), phir projection. Ulta order alag answer deta hai.
R − S me wo tuples bachte hain jo S me **exactly** (A aur B dono same) nahi hain. Phir $\pi_A$ duplicates hata deta hai.
R ke rows ek-ek karke S me dhundo: (1, x) S me hai, to hatega. Ab (1, y), (2, x), (3, z) check karo. Trap: pehle π lagakar phir minus karna.
db-trc-06: Quantifier **∃** hai aur condition me `e.sid = t.sid` hai. Dono ka matlab alag-alag padho.
∃e (P ∧ Q) = kam se kam ek e jo P aur Q dono satisfy kare. Yahan P = 'e isi student ka enrolment hai', Q = 'grade A hai'.
Pehle `e.sid = t.sid` ka role socho: ye e ko kis student se jodta hai? Phir grade wali condition jodo. Trap: ∃ ko 'har' padh lena.
db-trc-07: ∀ yahan Supplies ke rows pe chal raha hai, Parts pe nahi. Socho kis cheez ke baare me 'har ek' bola ja raha hai.
∀u (P(u) ⇒ Q(u)): har u jo P satisfy kare wo Q bhi kare. Agar koi u P satisfy hi na kare, to statement khud-ba-khud true (vacuous truth).
Ek supplier lo jiska Supplies me koi row nahi: `u.sid = t.sid` har u ke liye false hai, to implication kya banega? Trap: ise 'every red part' padh lena.
db-trc-08: ¬∃ ka matlab 'aisa koi nahi': koi D2 employee nahi hona chahiye jiski salary t ke barabar ya zyada ho.
¬∃s (D2(s) ∧ s.sal ≥ t.sal) ⇔ t.sal > har D2 salary ⇔ t.sal > max(D2 salaries).
D2 ke rows: e2 (60) aur e4 (40). Ab har employee ki salary is max se strictly compare karo. Trap: tie (60) wale ko bhi ginna.
db-trc-09: Target 'koi C nahi' hai. Har option ko is target se compare karo, khaaskar ∀ ke saath ⇒ hai ya ∧.
Duality: $\neg\exists e\,(P \land Q) \equiv \forall e\,(P \Rightarrow \neg Q)$. Aur ∀ ke saath ∧ ka matlab 'Enrolled ki har row' pe condition.
Option C test karo: Enrolled me kisi doosre student ka row ho to `e.sid = t.sid` false — tab ∧ wala ∀ kya dega? Option D ke liye A aur C dono grades wala student lo. Trap: ∀ ke saath ∧ likhna.
